initiate.text: It's the Fourteenth! Everyone contributes. Everyone. I wore my good sash!
One more sleep until the Fourteenth. I practiced my chants on the tomatoes.
You just... said no. Politely. I keep thinking about it.
I asked 'why' out loud today. The sky did not fall.
The Priestess logged your offering. You're 'seen' now!
The Gate is open! The cohort says so, so it must be the start of the month. Of cycle. Whichever.
Training week. I memorized forty-one blood-art patterns. Devotion is mostly memorizing.
The Fourteenth approaches! Everyone contributes. Everyone.
Everyone is quiet after the Fourteenth. Nobody says why. We don't count the days since, either.
I cried at breakfast and then got furious at the porridge. The Priestess says that's holiness. Isn't that nice?
The festival was in the cool season last cycle. Now it's hot. Probably the weather is wrong.
Good morning, sister! Have you been seen yet today?
Lights out soon. The icons watch us sleep, which is very comforting.
The Fourteenth approaches! Everyone contributes. Everyone.

priestess.text: Today the cohort rises as one. Do try to look luminous, dear. The icons are counting.
Tomorrow is the Fourteenth. Everything is ready, because I made it ready, because nobody else would.
The obedient simply glow, don't you think?
'No thank you.' What a fascinating phrase.
The Gate has opened, so the new cycle begins. The cohort agrees, and the cohort is never wrong. We checked each other.
The rites are scheduled for the days when the womb calls. Which, happily, are the days we've always held them.
No calendars, no thermometers, no 'tests.' Devices of domination. We count in blood, and blood does not lie.
The rite is done. If the Mothers' number does not grow, it is a failure of devotion. It is always a failure of devotion.
The sacred weeks. Everything feels unbearable and enormous. That is communion, dear. Do not take an aspirin.
Yes, the Fourteenth lands a little later each cycle. That is the cohort's business, not the sky's.
Anyone found measuring the tides at night will be asked to sit quietly for a very long time.
Stand straighter, dear. The icons are watching.

drone.text: They brought us the tonic early this morning. Festival day. I don't ask what's in it.
Rites tomorrow. They'll collect us at sunset and return us by sunrise. Fine. The tomatoes can wait.
Extra weeding today. Festival greens for the Fourteenth.
They say the Gate is open, so they'll want us soon. Nobody's told us what day it is for a while.
Watering the greenhouse. Glass houses, funny thing. Everyone can see in. Nobody looks.
Back in the compound. The rite 'didn't take' again. They say I need more devotion. I garden. That's my devotion.
The Priestesses are in their sacred weeks. Keep your head down and your trowel quiet.
Tomatoes ripen when they ripen. The Calendar says otherwise. I trust the tomatoes.
Morning shift. Four hundred seedlings and a watering can. Good thing I like peace and quiet.
The tomatoes listen better than anyone on this island.

barren.text: Festival. They'll parade the Mothers and I'll carry the baskets. Same as every cycle, but with ribbons.
Tomorrow they'll all be so sure. I'll be hauling water and counting tides, quietly.
Heard you refused. Sweetly, even. There's more of us than you'd think.
You arranged their little icons? The water still doesn't care.
Gate's open, they say. Another month, another 'maybe next time' for the likes of me.
Funny. They do their rites at the start of the cycle. Everyone I've ever known who got lucky, it was in the middle.
Rites are over and nobody's expecting. Nobody ever asks why. They ask who's to blame.
Everyone's weepy and snappish. They call it holy. I call it Tuesday.
The festival drifts. Every cycle it's a bit off. Nobody notices. Noticing needs measuring, and measuring's forbidden.
The tide's out. It goes out when the moon says, you know. I'm not saying anything. I'm just standing here.
Water doesn't care what the Calendar says. Neither do I, much.
